video_title: Fabolous On The Mixtape Era & How The Internet Blurred The Lines Between Mixtapes And Albums

quotes.speaker: Fabolous
quotes.summary_phrase: Fabolous on the evolution of mixtapes versus albums
quotes.excerpt: I think around once the internet came and even at beginning Drake, Kendrick Lamar 2010ish era, that's when I feel like the album started to blur into a mixtape was an album too.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: And that's what made albums and mixtape now different. Because now mixtape was just a mixtape and it was separate. Now it's kind of...

text_blocks.speaker: Fabolous
text_blocks.text: I think it's blurred. I think now it's close to the same thing. There's less separation. Mixtape also used to be more raw, more street, gritty, or more freestyle over other people's beats. I think around once the internet came and even at beginning Drake, Kendrick Lamar 2010ish era, that's when I feel like the album started to blur into a mixtape was an album too.

quotes.speaker: Fabolous
quotes.summary_phrase: Fabolous prefers his mixtapes over his studio albums
quotes.excerpt: I love your mixtapes better than the albums.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: Did you prefer mixtapes but knew that you had to do albums if you wanted to go global?

text_blocks.speaker: Fabolous
text_blocks.text: I'm going to be honest, right here on this show, I love your mixtapes better than the albums. The mixtape you spend, this is almost two different fabs at this point. Every artist don't get to do that. I think I had to do it because I had two lanes that I could, I literally came from the mixtapes, but then I had radio and girl song success too. So I had to make those records, but then I had to fulfill my mixtape audience, the guys like Mac who, this is what I want.

quotes.speaker: Fabolous

quotes.excerpt: When Make Me Better came out, I was actually in New York. And when I tell you Swizz Beatz played that mug like a hundred times in a row.

text_blocks.text: So when Make Me Better came out, I was actually in New York. And when I tell you Swizz Beatz played that mug like a hundred times in a row, I'm like, goddamn, I know the song, I know all the lyrics right now.

text_blocks.speaker: Fabolous
text_blocks.text: He played that back to back to back to back. That track went hard as shit. He played that when I was in New York. I remember that like it was yesterday.

quotes.speaker: Fabolous
quotes.summary_phrase: Fabolous on the mixtape era and song structure
quotes.excerpt: I think there's a lot of mixtapes that I even believe they provided the foundation of the success of me.

text_blocks.speaker: Fabolous
text_blocks.text: We was a little blurred on how, because in the mixtape era, me and Kiss would have went probably a different, but as it being on Def Jam and you got to make songs and songs they can structure to playlists and stuff like that, we had to just approach it a little bit different.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: So if it's not, then there's no competition.

text_blocks.speaker: Fabolous
text_blocks.text: I think there's a lot of mixtapes that I even believe they provided the foundation of the success of me. I would say mixtapes was the foundation of my so you knew I could rap. And then when me even doing radio songs, it was like, oh, he could do that too. But the mixtape was the foundation. Somebody like 50 Cent was another one who had mixtapes and it provided the foundation of his. And I don't think they say it much, but I think like Wiz Khalifa kind of had that in a sense too. He had like a mixtape catalog that provided the foundation and then he kind of spearheaded it from there.
